clue.text: Senseless comments bring ruin to a beautiful god

parts.note: Balder is the beautiful Norse god of light, son of Odin
to dash hopes is to bring them to ruin

explanation.surface: Someone destroys a lovely deity, apparently by talking nonsense at him.
explanation.walkthrough: Balder (also Baldur) is the Norse god famed for his beauty; DASH, to wreck, follows him.
explanation.definitionFit: Balderdash is nonsense, foolish talk with no sense in it.

clue.text: Wellington was given the sack

definitions.meaning: a wellington is a rubber ... named after the Duke
to be given the sack is to be dismissed from a job

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wellington' looks like the Duke or the city, but a wellington is a waterproof rubber boot; 'was given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear named after the Duke, and dismissal from work, as in being shown the door.

clue.text: German ruler with a serious understanding of the country

indicators.note: split as under-standing: in a down clue this piece stands beneath the other

parts.note: land means a country or nation
grave means serious or solemn

explanation.surface: A German leader with a sober grasp of his nation's affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'understanding' as 'under-standing': in a down entry, the serious word stands beneath the country word.
explanation.definitionFit: A landgrave was a count with territorial jurisdiction in the Holy Roman Empire, a German princely title.

clue.text: Finish doing a headstand

definitions.meaning: to finish somewhere is to wind up there eventually
upside down, with the bottom end pointing upwards

explanation.surface: Someone completes their routine by balancing on their head.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish in a place is to arrive there at last; a person upside down has their rear end in the air.

clue.text: Treble part Desmond hasn't the ability to follow

indicators.note: this piece comes after the shortened name, following it

parts.note: Des is the short form of the name Desmond
can't means is unable to

explanation.surface: Desmond is not able to sing the high harmony line.
explanation.definitionFit: A descant is a melody sung above the main tune, a high treble line.

clue.text: Cried out in the outhouse

indicators.note: the word out goes inside the outbuilding's synonym

parts.note: a shed is an outhouse, a small outbuilding

explanation.surface: Someone yelled from inside a garden building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cried out' looks like one phrase, but 'out' is the piece put in SHED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have cried is to have yelled or called loudly.

clue.text: Sound barrier

definitions.meaning: a deep resonant noise, as of a gun or drum
a floating barrier across a harbour or river mouth

explanation.surface: The bang an aircraft makes breaking through Mach 1.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the 'sound barrier' of supersonic flight; split it into two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A boom is a loud hollow noise, and also a chain or spar stretched across water to block ships.

clue.text: Preach for a zero interest charge

parts.note: the letter O resembles the figure zero
a rate is the percentage charged as interest

explanation.surface: A preacher sermonising in favour of interest-free loans.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal speech, to hold forth as a preacher does.

clue.text: Judging a fashion assessment

parts.note: mode means a fashion or style
a rating is an assessment of quality

explanation.surface: A critic evaluating a style trend.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderating is presiding over and judging, as an exam moderator does.

clue.text: Conventional style in the north of England

parts.note: stock means standard or conventional, as in a stock reply
ton is fashion or style, as in high society

explanation.surface: A traditional way of doing things found up north.
explanation.walkthrough: Stockton-on-Tees is a town in County Durham, north-east England; the definition is loose, naming only where the place is.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockton is a market town on the River Tees in north-east England.

clue.text: Had given an acknowledgment

explanation.surface: Someone had made a formal admission.
explanation.definitionFit: Possessed, and also admitted, an old sense of 'own' meaning confess.

clue.text: Employee of little standing requires secretarial skill

parts.note: short means of small height, little in stature
a hand is a worker, as in a farm hand

explanation.surface: A lowly employee needs typing and note-taking skills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of little standing' suggests low status, but it means small stature; 'requires' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorthand is a rapid writing system that secretaries used for dictation.

clue.text: Vegetable for the battery-house

definitions.meaning: the aubergine, as Americans call it
a factory where battery hens produce their output

explanation.surface: A vegetable suited to a battery farm.
explanation.walkthrough: A battery is a block of cages for laying hens, so a battery-house is a factory producing what the hens lay.
explanation.definitionFit: The aubergine is called this in America; the second reading is a factory turning out what hens lay.

clue.text: A man of honour always offers comfort

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: An honourable gentleman is ever ready to console.
explanation.walkthrough: CH, Companion of Honour, is a British award; 'offers' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone is to comfort or hearten them.

clue.text: Where the angler takes his catch out of harm's way

definitions.text: Where the angler takes his catch
definitions.meaning: a fish is removed from the barbed metal on the line

explanation.surface: A fisherman unhooks his catch safely.
explanation.definitionFit: The fish is taken from the barb; idiomatically, someone freed from trouble or responsibility.

clue.text: Charged a priest nothing

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
aught is a variant of naught, meaning nothing or zero

explanation.surface: A clergyman was billed nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' looks like a billing verb but defines the answer as 'charged with tension'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraught means filled or laden, as in a situation charged with anxiety.

clue.text: Gruff warning to cultivate heather

parts.note: to grow plants is to cultivate them
ling is the common heather of moorland

explanation.surface: A gardener is told off for planting heather.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog's low rumbling snarl is a rough warning sound.

clue.text: US city editor edited cross letter

indicators.note: edited signals that the letters of the word before are revised into a new order

parts.note: T is the letter shaped like a cross

explanation.surface: An editor revised a letter written by an angry correspondent in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edited' rearranges EDITOR to DETROI; 'cross' looks like 'angry' but describes the T-shaped letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Detroit is the Michigan city famous for car manufacturing.

clue.text: Stubborn stain to be removed

indicators.note: the letters of the stain are shifted and rearranged, so the word signals a reordering

explanation.surface: A stubborn mark that needs cleaning off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' rearranges STAINTOBE; the surface of a stubborn stain fits neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinate means refusing to change one's mind, stubborn.

clue.text: Definitive job in Royal Mail

parts.note: 'the' is the definite article
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: A permanent position with the national postal service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Definitive' looks like a postage stamp term, but it gives the definite article THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's postal service is Royal Mail; letters are sent by post.

clue.text: To the County Council a word of thanks for a noted performance

parts.note: CC is the abbreviation for County Council
ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: A thank-you to the local council for a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: A County Council is English local government; 'ta' is British slang for thanks. 'noted' means set to music.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a virtuoso keyboard piece, a musical work played from notes.

clue.text: Listens to a melody associated with evil

parts.note: a tune is a melody
sin is wrongdoing, evil

explanation.surface: Someone hears a wicked song.
explanation.definitionFit: To tune in is to listen to a radio station or broadcast.

clue.text: Essay about ancient drama

indicators.note: the attempt word goes around the word for old

parts.note: to essay is to try or attempt
aged means old, ancient

explanation.surface: A school paper on classical theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essay' looks like a written piece, but here it is the verb meaning attempt, and 'about' wraps it round the word for old.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedy is a serious play ending in disaster, a form of drama.

clue.text: Praise former tax reduced by a pound

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: the tax is cut by taking off the symbol for pounds

parts.note: a toll is a charge or tax for passage
L, from Latin libra, stands for a pound

explanation.surface: Applauding a tax cut of one pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced by' removes one L from TOLL, leaving TOL.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly.

clue.text: Yours has scant energy

parts.note: thin means sparse or scant
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Your stamina is in short supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Thine is the archaic second-person possessive, as in 'thy kingdom, thy will'.

clue.text: The parson takes tea without milk or sugar

parts.note: cha (char) is British slang for tea
plain means unadorned, with nothing added

explanation.surface: A vicar drinks his tea black and unsweetened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cha' or 'char' is British informal for tea; 'takes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a clergyman attached to an institution, like a parson.

clue.text: Inclined to get an article in fast

indicators.note: the article goes inside the fasting season

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone tended to write a piece during a fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Leant means sloped or tilted, inclined at an angle.

clue.text: Leather is best

definitions.meaning: to leather is to thrash or whip
to best someone is to defeat them

explanation.definitionFit: To thrash someone soundly, and to defeat or outdo them.

clue.text: Direct trainee to make amends

indicators.note: to amend is to alter, so these letters are changed into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A trainee is told to apologise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make amends' rearranges TRAINEETO; it looks like an apology.
explanation.definitionFit: To orientate is to point in a particular direction, to direct.

clue.text: On the alert for a funeral party

parts.note: a wake is a gathering after a death

explanation.surface: Staying watchful at a gathering of mourners.
explanation.definitionFit: Awake means not asleep, watchful and alert.

clue.text: Bitter lament by the bereaved

definitions.meaning: a wail of grief, especially Irish mourning

explanation.surface: Mourners wail a sharp, bitter dirge.
explanation.definitionFit: A biting cold wind; and an Irish wail for the dead.

clue.text: The simple way to acquire wealth

definitions.text: The simple way to acquire wealth

parts.words: The simple way to acquire wealth
parts.note: read as a road named for being simple, where life is comfortable and money is plentiful

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is also a charade of 'simple' and 'way' (a road), but the whole clue describes the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on this road is to live in comfort and affluence.
